speakingHero.label: Speaking
speakingHero.headline: What your people walk away with
speakingHero.intro: Every presentation starts from lived experience, Jean Claude’s own, and is shaped to your room.

talksSection.heading: Topic presentations
talksSection.intro: Each one starts from a real story, then leads somewhere your people can act on.

presentations.title: More than Medicine
presentations.text: Diagnosed with chronic kidney disease in 2019 while living in Rwanda, Jean Claude received a kidney transplant in Egypt in 2020 and immigrated to Canada in 2022. In 2023, he returned to dialysis after his transplanted kidney failed. Through his journey as a kidney patient, transplant recipient, and newcomer, he shows that good care depends on more than treatment: it also depends on dignity, communication, and community.
presentations.leave: Audiences leave with a clearer understanding of the human side of chronic illness and of what patients need beyond the clinic.

presentations.title: Why Belonging Matters?
presentations.text: Arriving in Canada with hope of rebuilding his life, Jean Claude had to navigate a new healthcare system while adapting to life as a newcomer. He explains how belonging shapes whether people feel safe seeking care, speaking up, and staying connected to support.
presentations.leave: Audiences leave with practical ways to make their organizations and communities more welcoming to newcomers, immigrants, and refugees.

presentations.title: Leadership Through Lived Experience
presentations.text: From founding Love the Kids Rwanda in 2015 to using film and writing against gender-based violence, to living with kidney disease in a new country, Jean Claude has led through some of life’s hardest transitions. He shares how lived experience builds credibility, empathy, and resilience in leaders.
presentations.leave: Audiences leave with ways to turn their own challenges into purpose and to lead others with greater understanding.

presentations.title: From Personal Story to Community Action
presentations.text: Jean Claude’s experience led him to launch Sounds From a New Home in 2025, an Ottawa-based initiative that uses storytelling, peer education, counselling, and community events to support newcomers living with chronic illness. He shows how a personal story can grow into a program and how partnerships across healthcare, the arts, and community groups multiply its impact.
presentations.leave: Audiences leave with a plan for moving from sharing a story to creating change.
